variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: An ML data pipeline is a repeatable system that turns raw observations into versioned datasets, features, and quality evidence that models can safely consume. It coordinates what data is read, which transformations run, when outputs become visible, and how a result can be reproduced later.
variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Treat every stage as a data contract”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Identity
pairs.detail: Use a stable record key plus an interval, partition, or offset range.
pairs.explanation: Use a stable record key plus an interval, partition, or offset range. A wall-clock run timestamp alone cannot identify the intended data.

pairs.label: Schema
pairs.detail: Version field names, types, nullability, units, categorical vocabularies, and semantic constraints.
pairs.explanation: Version field names, types, nullability, units, categorical vocabularies, and semantic constraints.

pairs.label: Completeness
pairs.detail: Define expected partitions, minimum row coverage, lateness policy, and the evidence required before publication.
pairs.explanation: Define expected partitions, minimum row coverage, lateness policy, and the evidence required before publication.

pairs.label: Lineage
pairs.detail: Attach input versions, code version, parameters, run identity, quality results, and output location.
pairs.explanation: Attach input versions, code version, parameters, run identity, quality results, and output location.

variants.hint: Give each part the one job only it can do, then rule out the rest. The core invariant is replay equivalence: the same logical input interval, transformation version, schema contract, and parameters should produce the same committed output.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Identity: Use a stable record key plus an interval, partition, or offset range. Schema: Version field names, types, nullability, units, categorical vocabularies, and semantic constraints. Completeness: Define expected partitions, minimum row coverage, lateness policy, and the evidence required before publication. Lineage: Attach input versions, code version, parameters, run identity, quality results, and output location.

variants.title: Give each part its job

It coordinates what data is read, which transformations run, when outputs become visible, and how a result can be reproduced later.
variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Separate event time from processing time”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Assign event time
pairs.detail: Take the timestamp from the event's domain contract rather than from the worker clock whenever the source can provide it reliably.
pairs.explanation: Take the timestamp from the event's domain contract rather than from the worker clock whenever the source can provide it reliably.

pairs.label: Group into windows
pairs.detail: Place records into fixed, sliding, or session windows according to the business question being answered.
pairs.explanation: Place records into fixed, sliding, or session windows according to the business question being answered.

pairs.label: Advance a watermark
pairs.detail: Estimate how complete event-time progress is.
pairs.explanation: Estimate how complete event-time progress is. A watermark is an operational estimate, not proof that no earlier record can arrive.

pairs.label: Apply lateness policy
pairs.detail: Update a prior result, emit a correction, quarantine the record, or drop it with a measured reason after the allowed-lateness boundary.
pairs.explanation: Update a prior result, emit a correction, quarantine the record, or drop it with a measured reason after the allowed-lateness boundary.

variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: An ML data pipeline is a repeatable system that turns raw observations into versioned datasets, features, and quality evidence that models can safely consume. It coordinates what data is read, which transformations run, when outputs become visible, and how a result can be reproduced later.
variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Build retry-safe partition commits”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Stable run identity
pairs.detail: Derive identity from the dataset, logical interval, transform version, schema version, and parameters.
pairs.explanation: Derive identity from the dataset, logical interval, transform version, schema version, and parameters. Keep attempt number separate.

pairs.label: Shadow then publish
pairs.detail: Write to a temporary location, validate the complete result, and atomically swap a manifest or pointer that readers resolve.
pairs.explanation: Write to a temporary location, validate the complete result, and atomically swap a manifest or pointer that readers resolve.

pairs.label: Deterministic replacement
pairs.detail: Replace one partition or merge by a stable record key.
pairs.explanation: Replace one partition or merge by a stable record key. Blind append turns ordinary task retries into duplicate data.

variants.prompt: Why does a streaming aggregation need event time and a lateness policy?

Processing time and event time can diverge, so a window needs rules for completeness and later corrections

Late records are always invalid
